facts.F56: Maintainer 2026-11-17: a named Cycle Time definition uses the same rule as the default: its UNPL is computed the same way (XmR, same baseline) over that definition's Cycle Times. The outlier rule must be designed as a replaceable definition (e.g. a strategy/policy passed in), so another outlier definition can be supplied later without reworking callers; still no user configuration now.
facts.F57: Where the rule lives: the outlier rule moves to the backend, Flow metrics module, behind a replaceable definition. Domain interface ICycleTimeOutlierDefinition (Modules/FlowMetrics/Domain/CycleTimeOutlierDefinition.cs) has one method: OutlierVerdict Judge(IReadOnlyList<int> baselineCycleTimes, IReadOnlyList<CycleTimeObservation> shown). The only implementation now is UpperNaturalProcessLimitOutlierDefinition, registered once as a singleton in Program.cs next to the metrics services and injected by constructor into TeamMetricsService and PortfolioMetricsService. A later definition is supplied by registering another implementation; the route, the DTO, the services and the frontend do not change. The frontend keeps no rule: it partitions the plotted items by the outlier ids of the verdict. Confirms the DISCUSS proposals: limit = the Cycle Time PBC UNPL (average + 2.66 x average moving range of the baseline Cycle Times, configured baseline or else the selected range), compared unrounded; only above-UNPL sets an item apart; no silent 5 x median fallback.
facts.F58: Carriers and owners. Domain (Modules/FlowMetrics/Domain): UpperNaturalProcessLimit value object in XmRCalculator.cs, holding the unrounded double, built by XmRCalculator.UpperNaturalProcessLimitOf(int[] baseline) and answering IsExceededBy(int days) as days > limit; XmRCalculator.Calculate and its large-change rule use the same object, so the PBC marker and the outlier rule share one formula and one comparison. OutlierVerdict closed choice (abstract record with two cases): Limited(UpperNaturalProcessLimit Limit, IReadOnlyList<int> OutlierWorkItemIds) and NoLimits. CycleTimeObservation(int WorkItemId, int Days) record. Application (Modules/FlowMetrics/Application): GetCycleTimeOutliers(owner, startDate, endDate, int? definitionId) on ITeamMetricsService and IPortfolioMetricsService, built once in BaseMetricsService.BuildCycleTimeOutliers: it resolves the baseline with ResolveBaseline, collects baseline and shown Cycle Times with the same window, filter (Cycle Time > 0) and order as BuildCycleTimeProcessBehaviourChart (a named definition uses each item named duration, items without one are skipped), and asks the injected definition; cached through GetFromCacheIfExists with a key that includes the definition id. API: GET cycleTime/outliers?startDate&endDate&definitionId on TeamMetricsController and PortfolioMetricsController, next to cycleTime/pbc, under the same RbacGuard read requirement; DTO CycleTimeOutliersDto (API/DTO) with Status (CycleTimeOutlierStatus Ready or NoLimits, serialised as a string), UpperNaturalProcessLimit (double or null) and OutlierWorkItemIds (int array). Frontend: ICycleTimeOutliers model, MetricsService.getCycleTimeOutliers for Team and Portfolio, and a keyed TanStack query in the chart. Per-process state: none new beyond the existing metrics cache; the switch is React component state only.
facts.F59: Rejected: reuse the existing cycleTime/pbc answer in the frontend. Its UNPL is rounded to whole days while the chart classifies with the unrounded value, so a frontend comparison disagrees at the boundary (see refuted law); it has no named-definition variant; and its LargeChange marker also covers points below the lower limit. Rejected: recompute XmR in TypeScript, a second owner of the same rule. Rejected: a frontend strategy object, because the named Cycle Times and the baseline rules live in the backend. ADR-282 decisions 1 to 3 (5 x median, frontend fiftiethPercentile) are superseded for the Cycle Time scatterplot by the new ADR; its decisions 4 to 7 (filter outliers out of the series, edge markers, chip and list, statistics untouched) stay.

facts.F61: Loading and failure looks: the verdict is a keyed TanStack query owned by the chart, key [ownerKind, ownerId, startDate, endDate, definitionId or default], fetched whenever the scatterplot is shown, independent of the PBC widget. While it is pending or failed no item is set apart and no count is shown: pending reuses the chip loading wording (Outliers / Outliers, loading, disabled) and the chart reports loading up to its WidgetShell frame through the existing widget status channel, so the frame dims under its spinner; a failed query reports failure so the frame shows its could-not-load look. A late answer for an older key never lands (the key differs; no placeholder data from another key). Confirms the DISCUSS proposal.
facts.F62: No usable limits: the verdict is NoLimits when the resolved baseline is invalid (missing, or shorter than 14 days) or holds fewer than 2 positive Cycle Times (the PBC then draws UNPL = the single value or 0 and marks nothing). The chart then sets no item apart, draws every item with the pre-outlier axis, shows no count chip and shows in the chip place the text: No outliers: the {Cycle Time} process behaviour chart has no limits for this date range. The info popover says outliers need those limits. Never a fallback to 5 x median. Confirms the DISCUSS proposal.
facts.F63: Wording (Terminology words): help sentence An outlier is a closed {Work Item} whose {Cycle Time} is above the upper natural process limit of the {Cycle Time} process behaviour chart for this date range. List title {Work Items} with a {Cycle Time} above the upper natural process limit ({N} days), where N is the unrounded limit shown with at most one decimal (30.6, 30), so the stated limit and the listed set never disagree. Confirms the DISCUSS proposal with that precision.
facts.F64: Formal verification: the claims are pure, finite, request-response functions with no concurrency, waiting or recovery (one verdict per request). Claim-to-checker: outlier membership and NoLimits laws -> executable example tables at the application-service port plus a fast-check property on the frontend partition; no Quint/TLA+/Agda model was authored or run because the root context for this feature directed no formal model checking and a short algebraic note; the formal-proof axis of these claims is INDETERMINATE (not executed), never PASS. Liveness is not applicable: no state machine, no retry and no waiting; each request is a finite computation over a bounded list.
facts.F65: Named Cycle Time definitions use the same rule (maintainer, Confirmed): baseline dates resolved as for the default; values are each item named duration over the baseline window; Cycle Times of 0 and items without a named value are skipped, as the PBC skips 0-day items. An unknown or invalid named definition yields NoLimits; the chart already resets such a selection to the default.
